sections.overview: The Yellow Wagtail is a strongly migratory wagtail of open country; it is smaller and more yellow below than the White Wagtail described in the neighbouring profile.
sections.identification: Males are generally yellow below and greenish above, but head pattern varies widely among subspecies; females and juveniles are less distinctive.
sections.habitat: It breeds in wet grassland, pastures and hay meadows, and also uses arable farmland; outside the breeding season it winters in sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.diet: It forages on the ground for insects, often in grassland or near livestock.
sections.behavior: This is a long-distance migrant, returning to European breeding grounds in spring and moving south to Africa for winter.
sections.reproduction: In the UK account, it nests on the ground and can raise two broods where suitable habitat is available.
sections.ecology: Its yellow underside and smaller size distinguish it from the larger black, white and grey White Wagtail; head pattern within Yellow Wagtails varies with subspecies.
sections.conservation: The RSPB places the UK population on its Red List after serious breeding declines; this regional trend is linked to farmland change and is not a global category.
